subject: Audit & access logs — retention window, residency, and export options
messages:
From: Jake Reynolds <jake.reynolds@acme-health.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Marta Gomez <marta.gomez@gridadvices.io>
Date: 2026-11-04T23:12:00Z
Subject: Question: audit/access log retention and exports

Hi Monica,

We're preparing for an upcoming compliance review at Acme Health and need a clear statement of how Redwood handles audit and access logs for our hosted instance. A few specific asks: 
- Default retention period for audit logs and for access (API/auth) logs.
- Can we export raw logs (format and frequency) and push to our S3 bucket or get ad-hoc exports?
- Is log storage region-bound (i.e., can logs be kept only in EU region for EU customers)?
- For deletion requests (e.g., a user requests removal of their activity), what is the mechanism and SLA?

If it's easier, happy to hop on a short call. We may also need a sample export snippet to show our reviewers.

Thanks,
Jake
Jake Reynolds
Head of IT Compliance, Acme Health

From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Jake Reynolds <jake.reynolds@acme-health.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-05T01:22:00Z
Subject: Re: Question: audit/access log retention and exports

Hi Jake — thanks for the questions. Below is a concise Q&A and what we can deliver out-of-the-box versus via ops support. 

1) Default retention windows
- Hosted (standard): audit and access logs retained for 90 days by default.
- Hosted (enterprise tenants with contract): configurable up to 365 days (requires Dedicated or Enterprise add-on).
- Dedicated/Private: retention is configurable by customer policy; our standard guidance is 90/365/730 depending on contract.

2) Export capabilities and formats
- Scheduled exports: we support daily exports of audit/access logs in JSON Lines (NDJSON) and CSV. These are pushed to a customer-configured S3-compatible bucket (AWS S3, GCS via interoperability, or any S3-compatible endpoint).
- Ad-hoc exports: for compliance requests we can generate ad-hoc time-bounded exports (specific time range) and provide a signed S3 link or upload to your bucket. Typical SLA for ad-hoc exports is 48 hours for ranges under 30 days; larger ranges are estimated case-by-case.
- Streaming/real-time: we provide a near-real-time streaming webhook (event-forwarder) for audit events for Dedicated/Private customers.

3) Residency (region) behavior
- Logs are stored in the deployment's region by default. For our hosted product we have region controls (us-east, eu-west, asia-southeast). If your tenancy is in the EU region, logs remain in EU storage by default.
- For customers requiring strict residency, we recommend Dedicated or Private deployment; we also offer a hosted EU-only option for enterprise accounts.

4) Deletion / selective removal
- Deleting logs: deletion follows the configured retention policy. For ad-hoc deletions (e.g., a data-subject access request), we can extract and redact user-identifying fields and remove matching entries from stored exports; permanent deletion from primary store is handled by the ops team and is documented in an auditable deletion ticket.
- SLA: standard handling time for ad-hoc deletion requests is 72 hours once validated and approved by the customer's compliance contact; legal holds override deletion until cleared.

5) Provenance & audit trail
- All export and deletion actions are recorded in an immutable audit chain (separate admin audit log) that shows who requested the export/deletion, time range, and artifact location.

Attachments: I attached our lightweight runbook (audit_export_runbook.pdf) and a small sample (sample_audit_snippet.jsonl). Also included is a CSV example for reviewers (redwood_audit_csv_example.csv).

If you want columns/fields mapping, here's the quick field list in the export: timestamp, event_type, user_id (hashed by default for hosted), principal_type, resource, action, request_id, ip_address (redacted by policy), region, raw_payload (full event JSON).

If you want, Laura can confirm the S3 ACL/permissions specifics and provide sample IAM role or presigned URL guidance.

Thanks,
Rachel Kim
Director, Security & Compliance, Redwood Inference
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Jake Reynolds <jake.reynolds@acme-health.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-05T10:18:00Z
Subject: Re: Question: audit/access log retention and exports

Hi Jake — quick ops notes to make the export work seamless: 
- For daily pushes we provision a dedicated prefix in your bucket (e.g., s3://acme-health-redwood/audit/YYYY/MM/DD/) and uploads are atomic (multipart then rename).
- We support server-side encryption (SSE-S3 or SSE-KMS) and can accept uploads into a customer-managed KMS key for Private/Dedicated deployments.
- Presigned URLs vs IAM role: we prefer an IAM role assumption model for recurring exports (more secure), we can provide the trust policy and a sample CloudFormation template.
- Export size/throughput: typical daily export for medium tenants is ~1-3 GB; for large customers we recommend lifecycle policies (move to Glacier after 90 days).

If you'd like, we can schedule a 30-minute walkthrough to go over the bucket setup and provide a test export (we can drop a test file into your bucket within 24 hours once credentials are in place).

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Sr. Site Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
To: Jake Reynolds <jake.reynolds@acme-health.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>

Date: 2026-11-05T19:03:00Z
Subject: Re: Question: audit/access log retention and exports

Jake — one legal note to flag before any deletion work proceeds: if there are outstanding legal holds or ongoing investigations, those takes precedence and we cannot permanently delete records until cleared. For GDPR-related subject requests, we require validated proof of identity and an authorization point from your compliance team; once validated we'll follow the 72-hour operational SLA Rachel mentioned.

If Acme expects routine long-term retention requirements, let's document that in the contract amendment so we can extend the storage SLA and retention window (and include any required encryption/KMS constraints). Monica — can you pick this up with Jake and propose timing for the call?

-David
David Kim
VP Legal, Redwood Inference
